head_at_save_start: fdbdc0e Record worker tuning and scatter x16 experiments
request: Save current progress after real G11 packed-NVFP4 FlashInfer-aligned MoE work.
goal: Implement an in-repo CUDA kernel aligned with flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe for real TP=1 G11 packed NVFP4 MoE, and beat FlashInfer performance.

source_state.status: Stable committed source kept. Negative experiments are reverted. This checkpoint intentionally adds no kernel code changes.

recent_rejected_experiments.summary: splitcol_warpshuffle was faster in standalone GEMM2 but failed end-to-end correctness. postldsync had intermittent pass/fail behavior. Keep stable postsync default.
Padding-zero path was correct but regressed end-to-end latency; source reverted.
slots2 hidden-pack metadata was not stable because padding rows affected task08 GEMM1; generated GEMM2 epilogue sweeps hit timeouts.
GEMM1/GEMM2 worker-cluster overrides and final-scatter x16 did not improve the best stable end-to-end result.

untracked_files_policy.status: Leave untracked profile/log outputs and the unrelated nested kernel_opt_fused_moe_pes worktree uncommitted.
untracked_files_policy.reason: They are temporary or historical artifacts; recoverable experiment conclusions are captured by committed memory records and selected tracked profiles.

recommended_next_steps: Try a swizzled-only SwiGLU/requant API that skips writing and clearing the unused linear mid_scale tensor, while preserving the old API for probes.
If pursuing the faster GEMM2 warp-shuffle variant, first localize full-output corruption by row, column, expert id, and CTA rank against the stable postsync output.
Larger gains likely require eliminating intermediate memory traffic, especially by fusing GEMM2 epilogue with weighted final scatter or removing the GEMM2 output round trip.
Continue verifying only against real FlashInfer and the true G11 packed NVFP4 + FlashInfer prepared-weight contract.
